scenarios.name: Founder interview: intro, basics, flowchart, sequence diagram

checks.them: Let's do something visual. Can you draw a flowchart of how a chat message goes from the user tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen in our app?

card.problem: Draw a flowchart of a chat message from the user tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen
card.adopted: Message saved locally and shown first, then a stream from the backend updates the screen piece by piece
card.heard: draw a flowchart, send tap to streamed reply on screen
card.say: I'll draw the main path first. The user taps send, and the app saves the message locally and shows it right away. Then it opens a stream to the backend, and the AI reply comes back in pieces. Each piece updates the screen, and the final piece closes the stream.
card.type: draw@chat send to streamed reply: flowchart TD ⏎ A[User taps send] --> B[Save message locally] ⏎ B --> C[Show message on screen] ⏎ C --> D[Open stream to backend] ⏎ D --> E[AI reply arrives in pieces] ⏎ E --> F[Update screen per piece] ⏎ F --> G[Stream ends]
card.then: Next, I'd add what happens when the connection drops mid-stream.

checks.them: What happens in that flow if the network drops halfway through the reply? Add it to the diagram.

card.problem: Draw a flowchart of a chat message from the user tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen
card.adopted: Message saved locally and shown first, then a stream from the backend updates the screen piece by piece
card.constraints: ["If the network drops halfway through the reply, the diagram must show that path"]
card.heard: network drops halfway through the reply
card.say: Right, so the stream can end badly, not just cleanly. I'll add that path to the diagram. If the connection drops, the stream ends with an error, not a normal end. The app keeps the pieces it already saved, so the user still sees the partial reply. Then it shows a "connection lost" state with a retry button.

card.then: Next, I'd say where the partial reply is stored, so it survives the screen closing.

checks.them: Good. Now a different one: draw me a sequence diagram of login, including what happens when the access token expires and the app refreshes it.

card.problem: Draw a sequence diagram of login, including what happens when the access token expires and the app refreshes it
card.adopted: App logs in, stores access and refresh tokens, and on a 401 refreshes the token then retries the call once
card.heard: new task — sequence diagram of login with token refresh
card.say: Okay, that's a separate flow, so I'll start a new diagram. The app sends the login request, and the server returns an access token and a refresh token. The app saves both, then uses the access token on later calls. When a call comes back as expired, the app sends the refresh token, gets a new access token, and repeats the failed call once.
card.type: draw@login sequence: sequenceDiagram ⏎ participant App ⏎ participant Server ⏎ App->>Server: Login with credentials ⏎ Server-->>App: Access token + refresh token ⏎ App->>Server: API call with access token ⏎ Server-->>App: 401 token expired ⏎ App->>Server: Refresh with refresh token ⏎ Server-->>App: New access token ⏎ App->>Server: Retry the same API call ⏎ Server-->>App: 200 OK
card.then: Next, I'd cover what happens if the refresh itself fails, and how two calls at once share one refresh.
